key_insight: An RL-based framework that directly targets parameter-robust 'avoid' (safety) problems, learning controllers that remain safe across unknown system parameters while also detecting when safety is infeasible.
problem_solved: Bridges the mismatch between standard RL (which optimizes expected returns under a training distribution) and reachability/avoid objectives by producing policies that prioritize worst-case safety and by identifying cases where no safe policy exists under parameter uncertainty.
method: Formulate the avoid/reachability objective under parameter uncertainty and unknown feasibility, reframing it as a parameter-robust RL problem.

Train policies with a robustness-aware objective (worst-case or distributionally robust survival) while simultaneously estimating conservative safe sets or certificates to avoid overconfident failures.
Integrate a feasibility-detection mechanism that flags infeasible instances and guides conservative behavior or safe fallback controllers.
impact: Gives practitioners a practical way to deploy RL controllers that maintain safety across uncertain hardware/environment parameters and avoids silent failures by signaling when safety cannot be guaranteed.
visual_elements: State-space diagram showing safe/unsafe regions and an expanding conservative safe set under parameter uncertainty
Flowchart of the algorithm: robust RL training loop + feasibility detector + safe fallback
Heatmap or contour plot of safety probability across parameter values comparing standard RL vs. parameter-robust RL
Icon set: shield (safety), warning flag (infeasible detection), gear (hardware/parameters), chart (robust performance)
paper_title: Solving Parameter-Robust Avoid Problems with Unknown Feasibility using Reinforcement Learning
paper_authors: Oswin So, Eric Yang Yu, Songyuan Zhang, Matthew Cleaveland, Mitchell Black
